Field Definitions.Question: What is driving the need for a new ERP?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The forces actively pushing the company to change systems now: growth, acquisition, system end-of-life, new leadership, audit or compliance pressure, investor requirements. This is CATALYST territory: things happening that drive change. Synthesized from business_catalysts rows; not captured as its own field.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Summary (generated). Underlying catalysts extracted per the Catalyst entity definition on the Core Entities tab.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: what's prompting this; why now; we just acquired; our PE firm wants; QuickBooks is breaking; new CFO came in; auditors flagged
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Generic dissatisfaction without a driving force ('we hate our system') is a pain, not a catalyst. Consequences of NOT changing belong to compelling event, not here.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Our PE sponsor closed two add-ons this year and wants consolidated reporting by Q3' -> catalysts: PE acquisition activity; investor reporting mandate.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Closing the books is painful' -> pain point, not a driver. Do not write a catalyst from pain alone.

Field Definitions.Question: What problems are you trying to solve today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The specific operational and financial problems the prospect states they experience. RENDERS deal_pain_points; never captured as a parallel field. Each problem must be extracted as a pain point per the Pain Point entity definition.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Rendered list from deal_pain_points (no direct storage).
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: the problem is; what kills us is; we waste; we can't see; takes us forever to; error-prone; manual
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Solution wishes ('we want dashboards') are ideal_solution, not problems. Hypothetical risks the prospect has not experienced are not pains.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'AP is all paper; my controller spends two days a week keying bills' -> pain: manual AP entry, quantified 2 days/week controller time.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'It would be nice to have better reporting' -> desire, route to desired_reporting, not a pain.

Field Definitions.Question: What does success look like with a new system?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The prospect's stated picture of a successful outcome after implementation: measurable targets (close in 5 days, one consolidated P&L) or capability statements (every entity manager self-serves reports). Prospect-stated only.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text. Keep measurable targets verbatim with numbers intact.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: success would be; in a perfect world after go-live; we'd know it worked if; our goal is to get close down to
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: The rep's pitch of outcomes is not the prospect's success definition. Vendor-agnostic future plans (hiring, expansion) are catalysts, not success criteria.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'If we can close in five days and stop the Excel consolidation, that's a win' -> success: 5-day close; eliminate Excel consolidation.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Rep: 'Most customers cut close time in half' Prospect: 'mm-hm' -> not the prospect's statement; do not write.

Field Definitions.Question: What would your ideal solution look like?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The prospect's description of the system characteristics they want: capabilities, architecture, experience. Maps to deal_analysis.ideal_solution (existing AE field); this definition hardens that extraction.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text (existing home: deal_analysis.ideal_solution).
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: ideally; what we're looking for is; has to have; must be cloud; needs to talk to
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Hard requirements with pass/fail weight are decision criteria, not ideal-solution color. Do not duplicate: if stated as 'must have or we won't buy', route to decision criteria.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Ideally everything lives in one cloud system the whole team can get into from anywhere' -> ideal: single cloud system, broad access.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'It must integrate with ADP or it's a non-starter' -> decision criterion (must-have), not ideal-solution color.

Field Definitions.Question: What do you need Sage Intacct to manage for you?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The functional scope the prospect expects the new system to own: which processes move into it (GL, AP, AR, inventory, projects, budgeting). Drives module recommendation.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List of functional areas, normalized to module vocabulary where the mapping is unambiguous; otherwise keep the prospect's words.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we need it to handle; it has to run our; we want to move X into it; everything except payroll
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Capabilities they explicitly want to keep elsewhere ('payroll stays in ADP') are exclusions; record those in notes, not the list. Rep-suggested scope unconfirmed by the prospect is not scope.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'We need GL, AP, and we want inventory in there too; payroll stays with Paychex' -> [GL, AP, Inventory]; note: payroll excluded (Paychex).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Rep: 'You'd probably want our planning module too' Prospect: 'maybe' -> not confirmed scope.

Field Definitions.Question: How many entities do you have?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Count of distinct legal entities (corps, LLCs, partnerships, holding companies) whose books are or will be maintained. Includes the parent when it keeps its own ledger. Canonical home: deal_sizing.entity_count.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Number. 'Parent plus N subs' = N+1. Range given: store the stated/current number, note the range. Planned entities recorded in notes as planned, never added to the count.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we have N entities; N LLCs; N companies; N sets of books; the parent and N subsidiaries; we consolidate N
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Locations, offices, branches, stores, and warehouses are NOT entities unless stated as separate legal entities. Customers' entities don't count. Future entities ('we'll spin up two more') are planned, not current.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'There's the holding company and then nine operating LLCs under it' -> 10.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We've got twelve locations across the Southeast' -> locations, not entities; do not write entity_count.

Field Definitions.Question: What revenue streams do you have?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The distinct ways the company earns revenue (product lines, service lines, recurring vs one-time, grants for nonprofits), as described by the prospect.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List. Keep the prospect's labels; note approximate mix percentages if stated.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we make money from; three lines of business; recurring revenue from; the rest is services; grants and donations
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Research-derived offerings not confirmed on a call keep source=research. Customer segments (who buys) are not revenue streams (what is sold).
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'About 70% is SaaS subscriptions, the rest is implementation services' -> [SaaS subscriptions ~70%, implementation services ~30%].
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We sell to mid-market healthcare companies' -> customer segment, not a revenue stream.

Field Definitions.Question: Is there shared ownership across entities?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether entities share common ownership (same parent, same owners, PE sponsor) versus independently owned entities that are merely managed together.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Boolean + ownership description in notes (who owns what).
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: all owned by; same parent; our PE firm owns; family owns all of them; common ownership
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Shared management or shared back office is not shared ownership. Minority stakes described vaguely: capture the quote, mark partial.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Same two partners own all nine companies' -> true; notes: two common individual owners.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We do the books for all of them' -> management relationship, not ownership; do not infer true.

Field Definitions.Question: Where are your entities located by country and currency?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Country (and state if stated) of each entity plus the functional currencies in play. Multi-currency is a first-order fit signal.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List of country/currency pairs. Normalize currency names to ISO codes (Canadian dollars -> CAD) but keep the quote verbatim.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: entities in; our Canadian company; we bill in euros; functional currency; everything's USD except
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Selling INTO a country is not an entity there. Travel or remote employees abroad are not entities. Currency of customers' payments is not necessarily a functional currency; capture the quote and mark partial if unclear.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Two US entities, one in Toronto that books in Canadian dollars' -> [US/USD x2, Canada/CAD x1].
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We have customers in Mexico' -> market, not an entity location.

Field Definitions.Question: Do you use a shared chart of accounts?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether entities run on one common chart of accounts versus separate charts per entity. Direct consolidation-effort signal.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Boolean + notes (e.g., 'mostly shared, two legacy entities differ').
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: same chart across; one COA; each company has its own chart; we standardized the chart
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Shared accounting STAFF is not a shared chart. 'Similar' charts is partial, not true; capture the hedge verbatim.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Everyone's on the same chart except the acquisition we haven't converted yet' -> partial; notes: shared except one un-migrated entity.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'One bookkeeper does all the entities' -> staffing, not chart structure.

Field Definitions.Question: How are you handling inter-entity accounting today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The current mechanics of intercompany transactions: due-to/due-from tracking, eliminations, intercompany billing, and the tooling (manual journal entries, Excel, system-supported).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text. Capture mechanism + tooling + pain markers verbatim.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: due to due from; eliminations; intercompany; we true up between companies; journal entries between entities; consolidate in Excel
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Consolidated REPORTING alone is not the intercompany process. If they say 'we don't really do intercompany', record that as the answer (it is a finding), not as not_discussed.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Eliminations are a spreadsheet Maria maintains; intercompany loans are due-to/due-from JEs we true up quarterly' -> manual Excel eliminations; quarterly due-to/due-from JEs.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We roll everything up for the board deck' -> reporting output, not the intercompany mechanics.

Field Definitions.Question: How many total users will be in the system?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Headcount needing transactional access to the new system (entry, approval, processing). Canonical home: deal_sizing.full_users. License-driving number.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Number. If split given (e.g., '10 in finance, 5 ops approvers'), sum for the field, keep split in notes. Ranges: store low end, note range.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: N people in the system; N users; N seats; the team that would touch it is N
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Total employee count is NOT user count; never substitute one for the other. Report-viewers stated separately route to reporting_readonly_users. Aspirational future users noted as planned.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Finance is eight, plus four project managers approving invoices, so twelve in the system' -> 12; notes: 8 finance + 4 PM approvers.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We're a 250-person company' -> employee count, not users; do not write.

Field Definitions.Question: How many users need access to reporting or read-only views?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Headcount needing only dashboards/reports without transactional access. Canonical home: deal_sizing.view_only_users.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Number. Same range/split handling as total_users.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: just need to see reports; read-only; dashboard access for; the entity managers just view; board members log in to look
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: People who RECEIVE emailed reports need no license; only those logging in count. If unclear whether viewers transact, mark partial with the quote.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Each of the nine GMs just needs to see their P&L, they won't enter anything' -> 9.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We send the board a monthly packet' -> distribution, not system access.

Field Definitions.Question: What accounting or ERP system are you using today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The current general ledger / ERP of record, per entity if they differ. Routes to company_systems (category=accounting, is_current=true). The displacement target.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: System name(s), normalized to canonical product names (QB Enterprise vs QBO matters). Per-entity mapping in notes when entities differ. Version/edition captured when stated.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we're on; we run; everything's in QuickBooks; the Canadian entity uses; still on Dynamics GP
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Systems they're EVALUATING are deal_competitors, not current systems. Systems used by their clients are not theirs. 'QuickBooks' alone is partial until edition is known; capture and note the edition gap.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Eight companies on QuickBooks Enterprise, the new acquisition is still on Sage 50' -> QuickBooks Enterprise (8 entities, current); Sage 50 (1 entity, current).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We're also looking at NetSuite' -> competitor, route to deal_competitors.

Field Definitions.Question: What payroll system are you using?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Current payroll provider/system. Routes to company_systems (category=payroll). Usually an integration endpoint, not a displacement target.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: System name normalized (ADP: which product if stated, e.g., Workforce Now). Multiple providers across entities listed per entity.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: payroll is through; we use ADP; Paychex handles; Gusto for the small companies
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: PEO relationships (TriNet, Insperity) are payroll+HR bundles; capture as stated and note PEO. A payroll system they're leaving is is_current=true with a note, not omitted.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'ADP Workforce Now for everyone except the Toronto entity, that's Ceridian' -> ADP Workforce Now (US entities); Ceridian (Canada).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Our clients mostly use ADP' -> their clients' systems, not theirs.

Field Definitions.Question: What order management system do you use?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The system where sales orders/fulfillment live today, if any. Routes to company_systems (category=order_management).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: System name; 'none/manual' is a valid answer worth recording when stated.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: orders come through; we process orders in; Shopify; Salesforce orders; it's all email and spreadsheets
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: CRM used for pipeline only is not order management; only where ORDERS are processed counts. E-commerce frontend vs OMS distinction: capture both if both named.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Orders land in Shopify, then we rekey them into QuickBooks' -> Shopify (order capture); note: manual rekey to accounting.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We track deals in HubSpot' -> CRM/pipeline, not order management.

Field Definitions.Question: What ticketing or operational systems are in place?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Industry-specific operational systems running the business (field service, PM software, EHR, ticketing, POS). Routes to company_systems (category=operational). Prime integration candidates.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List of system names with the prospect's description of role.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we run the business on; jobs are in; ServiceTitan; Procore; our POS is; tickets live in
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Productivity tools (email, Office, Slack) are not operational systems unless they ARE the operational process (e.g., 'dispatch runs on a shared Outlook calendar' is a finding worth capturing as manual-process).
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Field techs live in ServiceTitan; that's where every job and invoice starts' -> ServiceTitan (field service, invoice origin).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We use Teams to communicate' -> communication tool, skip.

Field Definitions.Question: What other systems integrate with accounting today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Which systems currently exchange data with accounting and HOW (native sync, middleware, CSV import, manual rekey). The 'how' is the finding. Routes to company_systems with integration_purpose.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List: system + direction + mechanism. Mechanism normalized to: native / middleware / file import / manual.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: syncs to; flows into QuickBooks; we export and import; Zapier moves; we rekey from
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Systems that SHOULD integrate but don't are is_needed=true, not current integrations; capture the gap explicitly. 'Integrated' without mechanism is partial; the mechanism question is the follow-up task.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Bill.com syncs natively; Shopify is a weekly CSV; everything else we key by hand' -> Bill.com (native); Shopify (file import, weekly); rest manual.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We'd want it to talk to ServiceTitan' -> needed integration (is_needed), not a current one.

Field Definitions.Question: What is your fiscal year structure (12 months, 13 periods, etc.)?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Fiscal year end and period structure (12 calendar months, 13 four-week periods, 4-4-5).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text, normalized: 'FYE <month>, <structure>'.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: fiscal year ends; we're a June year-end; calendar year; 13 periods; 4-4-5
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Tax year vs fiscal year can differ; if both mentioned, capture both labeled. Busy season is a separate field; don't conflate.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'September 30 year-end, regular monthly periods' -> FYE September, 12 months.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Taxes are due in April like everyone' -> tax filing, not fiscal structure.

Field Definitions.Question: What accounting method do you use (cash, accrual, or both)?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Basis of accounting: cash, accrual, or both (e.g., accrual books, cash tax reporting, or differing by entity).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Enum: cash | accrual | both, + notes on the split.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: accrual basis; cash basis; we book accrual but report cash for tax; the small entities are cash
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Cash FLOW concerns are not cash-basis accounting. If they say 'modified accrual' or hedge, capture verbatim as both/partial with the quote.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Accrual for the operating companies, the two little holding entities are cash' -> both; notes: accrual operating, cash holding.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Cash is tight this quarter' -> liquidity comment, not method.

Field Definitions.Question: How is payroll handled today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The payroll PROCESS: who runs it (in-house, provider, PEO), frequency, and how it lands in the GL (auto JE, manual JE, not at all). Complements system_payroll (the tool); this is the workflow.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: operator + frequency + GL posting mechanism.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we run payroll in-house; ADP runs it; biweekly; the JE comes over automatically; we key the payroll entry
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Don't duplicate the system name here without the process. HR functions (benefits, onboarding) are out of scope unless they affect the GL flow.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Biweekly through ADP; the GL entry is a manual JE our staff accountant builds from the register' -> ADP biweekly; manual JE posting (pain marker).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We use ADP' -> tool only; that's system_payroll, mark this partial pending process.

Field Definitions.Question: How do you manage sales tax?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: How sales tax is calculated, collected, filed, and in which jurisdictions: engine (Avalara), manual rate tables, accountant-handled, or not applicable (exempt/services).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: mechanism + jurisdictions count if stated. 'Not applicable' is a valid recorded answer.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: Avalara; we file in N states; rates are a spreadsheet; our CPA files; we're exempt; nexus
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Income tax and property tax are not sales tax. Worry about FUTURE nexus is a risk/catalyst, not the current process; capture separately.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'We collect in seven states, rates live in a spreadsheet and our controller files monthly' -> manual rate tables, 7 states, monthly self-filing.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Our CPA does our taxes' -> ambiguous (likely income tax); mark partial, follow-up task.

Field Definitions.Question: What does your internal control environment look like?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Approval thresholds, segregation of duties, audit posture (audited/reviewed/none), and known control gaps the prospect states.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text. Capture thresholds with numbers verbatim; audit status normalized: audited | reviewed | compiled | none.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we get audited; approval over $N; one person does everything; segregation; our auditors flagged
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: The prospect's aspiration for better controls is desired state. An audit FINDING is also a catalyst candidate; extract both (control fact here, catalyst entity separately).
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Annual audit; anything over $5k needs my sign-off, but honestly AP is one person end to end' -> audited; $5k approval threshold; SoD gap in AP (stated).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We should really have better controls' -> aspiration; mark partial, do not record as current state.

Field Definitions.Question: How long does it take you to close a month?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Business days from period end to close complete, current state, as stated by the prospect.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Number (business days). Weeks x5. Calendar references ('we close by the 20th') ~= that many calendar days, store as days with conversion noted. Ranges: midpoint, range in notes.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: takes us N days to close; we close by the Nth; close runs about N weeks; we're never done before the
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: TARGET close time ('we want 5 days') is success_definition, not current state. Year-end close duration is different; if both given, this field is the MONTHLY close, year-end in notes.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'We're usually done around the 18th' -> ~18 calendar days (~12-13 business); note conversion.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Goal is a five-day close' -> target, route to success_definition.

Field Definitions.Question: What are the biggest bottlenecks in the close process?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The specific close steps the prospect names as slowest/most painful (intercompany eliminations, bank recs, waiting on entity submissions, manual accruals). Each is also a pain-point candidate.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List of named bottlenecks, prospect's words. Each quantified bottleneck links to a deal_pain_points row (pain tie-in).
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: what slows us down is; we always wait on; the worst part is; recs take forever; chasing the entities
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: General 'close is slow' without a named step is close_duration_days color, not a bottleneck list entry. Rep-suggested bottlenecks ('I bet eliminations hurt') unconfirmed are nothing.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Honestly it's waiting on the nine entity P&Ls, then eliminations on top' -> [entity submission lag, manual eliminations]; both pain candidates.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Rep: 'Recs are probably the issue, right?' Prospect: 'I guess' -> weak confirmation; mark partial at most.

Field Definitions.Question: Where do delays typically occur?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: WHERE in the timeline delays cluster (first week waiting on data, last week in review) and WHY, when distinct from the named bottleneck steps.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text. If the prospect answers bottlenecks and delays as one answer, fill close_bottlenecks and mark this answered with the same quote rather than splitting artificially.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: the delay is always; we lose the first week to; review drags; waiting on the bank
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Don't force a distinct answer if the prospect treated bottlenecks and delays as one; duplicate-quote linking is correct, fabricated distinction is not.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'First ten days we're just waiting on statements and entity numbers' -> delays front-loaded: external data dependency.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: (no separate statement made) -> reuse bottleneck quote, do not invent a timeline.

Field Definitions.Question: What reports do you review most often today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The reports actually consumed on a rhythm (weekly flash, monthly P&L by entity, AR aging, job cost), as stated.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List: report + cadence if stated.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: every week I look at; the board gets; we live off the; AR aging every Monday
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Reports they WISH existed route to desired_reporting. Reports the REP suggests they need are nothing.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Monthly P&L by entity for the partners, AR aging weekly' -> [entity P&L (monthly), AR aging (weekly)].
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We'd love a real-time dashboard' -> desired_reporting.

Field Definitions.Question: What are you using those reports to analyze or decide?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The decisions the reports drive (pricing, staffing, which entity gets capital, collections priorities). Connects reporting pain to business impact.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text, tied to the named reports where possible.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we use that to decide; that tells us whether; drives our pricing; we staff off of
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Generic 'to run the business' is partial; probe-level specificity is the SC's FDC follow-up, not Lumen's guess.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'The job cost report decides which service lines we keep' -> job cost -> service-line continuation decisions.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We just need good reports' -> no decision stated; partial.

Field Definitions.Question: How confident are you in the data you are using?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The prospect's stated trust level in their numbers, with reasons (rekeying, version confusion, stale data). Low confidence statements are pain candidates.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text; capture hedges and qualifiers verbatim, they carry the signal.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: I don't fully trust; we second-guess; by the time we see it it's stale; pretty confident actually; two versions of the truth
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: The REP casting doubt on the prospect's data is not the prospect's confidence statement. Confidence about a single report generalized to all data: keep it scoped to what they said.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'By the time the P&L is done it's three weeks old, so nobody really trusts it for decisions' -> low confidence: staleness; pain candidate.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Rep: 'Spreadsheets always have errors' Prospect: (silence) -> nothing to extract.

Field Definitions.Question: How is your data segmented (classes, departments, crews, or other dimensions)?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The dimensions they slice data by today (or wish they could): class, department, location, project, crew, fund, program. Direct dimension-fit signal.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List of dimension names, current vs desired flagged per item.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we track by class; department-level P&L; we can't see it by location; everything's by job; funds and programs
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: QuickBooks 'class' abuse stories often mix current and desired; tag each dimension as current or desired per the quote, do not blend.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Classes for location today, but we really need service line too and QB can't do both' -> current: location (via class); desired: service line.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We have departments in the org chart' -> org structure, not data segmentation, unless they report by it.

Field Definitions.Question: What reporting would you ideally want to see?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Reports/visibility the prospect wants but lacks today. Demo-fuel and gap evidence.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List, prospect's words, with the why when stated.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: I wish I could see; what I really want is; if I could get; we can't produce
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Current reports route to key_reports. The magic-wand answer routes to wishlist_insight if framed as instant-insight; overlap is fine, link the same quote rather than duplicating text.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Consolidated cash across all nine entities, daily, without anyone building it' -> desired: daily consolidated cash view.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We get a weekly flash today' -> current report, key_reports.

Field Definitions.Question: What do you use Excel for today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The jobs Excel performs in their finance process (consolidation, eliminations, budgets, board packs, allocations). Each is a workload-displacement and pain candidate.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List of Excel jobs. Heavy ones link to pain rows when quantified.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: everything ends up in Excel; we consolidate in spreadsheets; the budget is a workbook; download to Excel and
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Light personal use ('I keep a to-do list') is noise; capture process-level Excel only.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Consolidation, eliminations, and the whole budget live in one giant workbook only Maria understands' -> [consolidation, eliminations, budgeting]; key-person risk noted; pain candidates.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'I like Excel' -> sentiment, skip.

Field Definitions.Question: Are you using pivot tables or offline analysis?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether analysis happens offline after export (pivots, manual mashups), indicating the system can't answer questions directly.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text/boolean + what they pivot on.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: export and pivot; download everything; mash it up offline; pivot tables on the GL dump
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Excel usage generally is the prior field; this is specifically the export-then-analyze pattern. If they answered it within excel_usage, link the same quote.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Every analysis starts with a GL export and a pivot' -> true; GL-export-driven analysis.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We use Excel for budgeting' -> excel_usage, not necessarily offline analysis.

Field Definitions.Question: What types of charts and graphs do you rely on?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Visualizations they actually use to consume data (trend lines, waterfalls, dashboards in a BI tool).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List; include the tool if named (Power BI, Tableau).
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we chart; trend lines on; our Power BI dashboard; the board likes the waterfall
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: A BI TOOL named here also writes a company_systems row (category=operational/BI); do both. Wishes route to desired_reporting.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Revenue trend and a cash waterfall in Power BI, refreshed manually' -> [trend, waterfall]; Power BI (company_systems); manual refresh noted.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Charts would be nice' -> desired, not current.

Field Definitions.Question: If you had a magic wand, what insight would you want instantly that you do not have today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The single instant-answer the prospect most wants. Highest-value demo moment per prospect; keep verbatim flavor.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text, near-verbatim.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: if I could snap my fingers; the one thing I'd want; instantly know; right now I can't tell you
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Do not summarize away the specificity; the verbatim phrasing is the demo script. Multiple wishes: keep the one they flagged as THE one, others to desired_reporting.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'I want to know today, not in three weeks, which entities are bleeding cash' -> instant entity-level cash burn visibility.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Better reporting overall' -> too generic; partial, follow-up task to sharpen.

Field Definitions.Question: Can you walk me through how you make money?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Narrative of the commercial model: what is sold, to whom, on what terms (contracts, projects, transactions, subscriptions). The container for the billing deep-dive.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text narrative; keep structure (X% of revenue from Y) verbatim.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: the way it works is; customers pay us; we bill; our model is; contracts run
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Overlaps revenue_streams (the list); this is the HOW narrative. Fill both from the same passage if it covers both; link the shared quote.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Annual SaaS contracts billed quarterly up front, services billed monthly on completion' -> model: annual SaaS / quarterly advance billing + monthly services billing.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Business is good this year' -> performance, not model.

Field Definitions.Question: How does invoicing and accounts receivable work today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: End-to-end current AR mechanics: invoice trigger, creation tool, delivery, terms, collections approach, cash application.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: trigger -> creation -> delivery -> terms -> collections -> cash app, as much as stated.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we invoice when; out of QuickBooks; net 30; collections is; we apply cash by
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Future-state desires are not the current process. Volume numbers stated here also fill deal_sizing.ar_invoices_monthly (same quote, both homes' provenance).
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Invoices go out of QB when the PM marks the job done, net 30, and our office manager chases everything over 45 days from a spreadsheet' -> trigger: PM completion; tool: QB; terms: net 30; collections: manual spreadsheet.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We want automated dunning' -> desired, route to ideal/desired.

Field Definitions.Question: What items are billable?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: What units appear on invoices: time, materials, milestones, subscriptions, expenses passed through, change orders.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List of billable unit types.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we bill for; time and materials; milestones; pass through expenses; change orders get billed
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Internal cost categories not billed to customers are out. If pass-through billing is mentioned with leakage ('we forget to bill expenses'), that is also a pain candidate.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'T&M for service work, fixed milestones on projects, and we pass through travel' -> [time, materials, milestones, expense pass-through].
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Payroll is our biggest cost' -> cost, not billable item.

Field Definitions.Question: Are any external systems feeding billing data?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Upstream systems where billable data originates (field service, PSA, e-commerce, time tracking) and how it reaches invoicing. Routes to company_systems with integration_purpose=billing-feed; this field holds the flow description.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: system -> mechanism -> invoicing. Systems named also write company_systems rows.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: billing comes out of; time flows from; ServiceTitan creates the invoice; we pull hours from
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Don't re-list the whole tech stack; only billable-data feeders. Manual rekey between the feeder and invoicing is the pain marker; capture it.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Hours live in Harvest, we export weekly and rekey into QB invoices' -> Harvest -> manual weekly rekey -> QB invoicing; pain candidate.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We use Slack' -> not a billing feed.

Field Definitions.Question: How are billing rates calculated?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: How prices/rates are determined: rate cards, per-contract rates, cost-plus, role-based rates, annual escalators.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text; capture escalators and exceptions verbatim.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: rate card; cost plus N%; by role; each contract has its own; rates bump N% annually
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Discounting behavior is adjacent but distinct; capture if volunteered, don't probe-fill. Wage rates (what they pay) are not billing rates (what they charge) unless cost-plus links them.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Role-based rate card, but legacy clients are grandfathered all over the place' -> role-based card + grandfathered exceptions (complexity marker).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We pay techs $40/hour' -> cost rate, not billing rate, unless cost-plus stated.

Field Definitions.Question: How are taxes applied to invoices?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: How sales tax lands on invoices specifically: engine-calculated, manual rates, customer-exempt handling. The invoice-level companion to sales_tax_management.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text. If fully answered within sales_tax_management, link the same quote rather than re-asking.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: tax gets added; Avalara calculates at invoice; we look up the rate; most customers are exempt
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Don't force separation from sales_tax_management when the prospect answered once; shared quote is correct.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'QB applies the rate we keyed per customer, and exemption certs live in a drawer' -> manual per-customer rates; physical cert management (pain candidate).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: (answered fully in sales tax field) -> link, don't duplicate.

Field Definitions.Question: What revenue recognition method do you use?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: How revenue is recognized: point-in-time, over-time/ratable, percentage-of-completion, milestone, completed-contract, cash. 606 posture if stated.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text normalized to method names; multiple methods per stream listed per stream.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we recognize; ratably; percentage of completion; when the job's done; 606; deferred revenue
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Billing timing is NOT recognition ('we bill quarterly up front' says nothing about rec). If they conflate billing and rec, capture the quote, mark partial, generate the follow-up task: this is a classic FDC clarification.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'SaaS is ratable over the contract, services we take as delivered' -> ratable (SaaS); as-delivered (services).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We bill annually in advance' -> billing terms; rec method still unknown; partial.

Field Definitions.Question: Is billing structured across entities or intercompany?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether entities bill each other or share customers (management fees, shared-service chargebacks, one entity invoicing on behalf of others).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text/boolean + structure description.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we bill between companies; management fee; entity A invoices for everyone; chargebacks
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Intercompany ACCOUNTING (due-to/due-from) is interentity_accounting_today; this is customer-facing or fee billing BETWEEN entities. Related quotes can link to both when they genuinely cover both.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'The management company bills each LLC a 3% fee monthly' -> true; monthly management-fee billing.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We true up loans between entities' -> intercompany accounting, not billing.

Field Definitions.Question: What does your end-to-end invoicing process look like?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The full walk from billable event to cash applied, including handoffs and people. The synthesis question; usually answered across several quotes.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text narrative assembled from quotes; every step must trace to a quote (multi-quote provenance allowed).
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: so the way an invoice happens is; from there it goes to; then accounting; finally we apply
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: This field accumulates; do not force completion in one call. Steps not yet described stay absent; never bridge gaps with assumed steps.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quotes across the call -> 'Job completed (ServiceTitan) -> office manager exports -> rekey to QB -> email PDF -> net 30 -> manual cash app from lockbox report' (each step quote-traced).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Filling 'then they presumably approve it' between two stated steps -> fabricated step; never write.

Field Definitions.Question: What bank are you using today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Primary operating bank(s). Feeds bank-feed compatibility checks.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Bank name(s); per-entity mapping if stated.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we bank with; accounts at; Chase for operating; the line is with
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Lenders that are not the operating bank are credit relationships; note separately. Personal banking references are noise.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Operating accounts at Truist, the acquisition still has its Wells accounts' -> Truist (primary); Wells Fargo (legacy entity).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Our line of credit is with a private lender' -> credit facility, note, not operating bank.

Field Definitions.Question: What credit cards are in use?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Corporate card programs in use (Amex, bank cards, Ramp/Brex-style platforms) and roughly who carries them. Spend-management platforms named here also write company_systems rows.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List of card programs; cardholder scope in notes.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: corporate Amex; everyone has a card; we moved to Ramp; bank-issued cards
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Personal cards used for business expenses is a finding (expense-process pain marker), capture it as stated. Card PROCESSING for customers (merchant services) is a different topic.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Fifteen managers carry Amex, plus the Ramp cards we just rolled out' -> [Amex (15 holders), Ramp]; Ramp -> company_systems.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We take Visa from customers' -> merchant acceptance, not corporate cards.

Field Definitions.Question: How do you feel about your current bank reconciliation process?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The prospect's stated experience of bank recs: effort, frequency, lag, and feeling. Sentiment fields capture the verbatim emotional register; it sells the demo moment.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text, near-verbatim. Quantified effort links a pain row.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: recs are a nightmare; takes N days; we're always behind on; honestly it's fine; my least favorite
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: The rep's characterization ('recs must be brutal') confirmed only by 'yeah' is weak; prefer the prospect's own words, mark rep-led confirmations partial.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Nine entities, nine recs, my senior loses a week every month to them' -> negative; ~1 week/month senior time; pain row linked.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Rep: 'Recs are painful, right?' Prospect: 'Sure' -> partial at most; no quantification.

Field Definitions.Question: How do you feel about your current credit card reconciliation process?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Same as bank_rec_sentiment, scoped to corporate card recs: receipt chasing, coding, statement matching.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text, near-verbatim. Quantified effort links a pain row.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: chasing receipts; coding the Amex bill takes; cardholders never submit; the statement rec is
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Expense-report pain overlaps expense_report_process; if one quote covers both, link it to both rather than splitting the sentence.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'The Amex bill is 400 lines and two days of asking people what they bought' -> negative; 2 days/month; pain row.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We pay the card on time' -> payment behavior, not the rec experience.

Field Definitions.Question: How does your payables process work for rent, utilities, and other recurring expenses?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: How recurring/predictable payables are handled: auto-pay, memorized transactions, manual entry each cycle.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: mechanism per recurring category as stated.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: rent is on autopay; we key utilities every month; memorized transactions; recurring bills
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: One-off vendor bills are bill_intake/vendor_payment territory; this field is the recurring subset. If the prospect doesn't distinguish, answer the general fields and mark this covered-by reference.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Rent autodrafts, utilities get keyed monthly by the AP clerk' -> rent: autopay; utilities: manual monthly entry.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We pay about 300 bills a month' -> volume, route to bills_per_period.

Field Definitions.Question: What does the approval process look like?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Bill approval workflow: who approves, thresholds, mechanism (email, system, verbal).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: approver chain + thresholds + mechanism. Thresholds verbatim.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: approvals go through; over $N needs; I sign every check; it's an email chain; no real approvals
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: 'No approvals' stated is a finding (control gap), record it. Purchase approvals (pre-spend) are purchasing_process; this is bill/payment approval (post-invoice).
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Anything over $2,500 comes to me by email, under that the controller just pays it' -> threshold $2,500; email-based; two-tier.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'POs need my sign-off' -> purchase approval, route to purchasing_process.

Field Definitions.Question: How are vendor bills paid today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Payment rails in use: check, ACH, card, wire, bill-pay platform, and rough mix.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List of methods + mix if stated. Platforms named (Bill.com, Melio) also write company_systems.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we cut checks; ACH through the bank; pay by card when we can; Bill.com pushes payment
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: How CUSTOMERS pay them is AR; this is outbound only. 'We should stop cutting checks' is desired state.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Probably 60% checks still, the rest ACH out of Bill.com' -> [check ~60%, ACH ~40% via Bill.com].
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Customers pay us by ACH mostly' -> AR side, skip here.

Field Definitions.Question: How do vendor bills get into the system?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: How bills arrive and get entered: email inbox, paper, OCR capture, vendor portals, manual keying.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: intake channel(s) + entry mechanism.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: bills come in by email; we key them; scanned and; AP inbox; someone types every invoice
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Capture TECHNOLOGY is the next field; if one quote answers both, link to both. Approval flow is separate.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Everything lands in an AP inbox and gets keyed by hand into QB' -> email intake; fully manual entry.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'I approve them in email' -> approval, not intake.

Field Definitions.Question: How many bills are you processing in a typical period?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Vendor bill volume per month. Canonical home: deal_sizing.ap_invoices_monthly.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Number per month. Weekly x4.33 noted; annual /12 noted. Ranges: midpoint, range in notes.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we process N bills; N invoices a month; a few hundred a month; N a week
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Customer invoices (AR) are the other direction; do not cross-write. 'A lot' is partial pending a number; create the follow-up task.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Call it 300, 350 bills a month across the group' -> 325; range noted.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We send about 200 invoices a month' -> AR volume, route to deal_sizing.ar_invoices_monthly.

Field Definitions.Question: What payment methods are you using?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Catch-all confirmation of payment rails if answered separately from vendor_payment_methods; otherwise covered-by that field.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Same normalization as vendor_payment_methods; merge rather than duplicate.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: (same as vendor_payment_methods)
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: This is a doc-level near-duplicate of vendor_payment_methods; extraction treats them as one fact with one home. Curation may merge the rows.
Field Definitions.Good Example: (merged with vendor_payment_methods)
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Writing different values to the two fields from one conversation -> forbidden; one fact, one home.

Field Definitions.Question: Are you using any technology to transcribe or capture bills?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether OCR/capture tooling exists (Bill.com capture, Dext, Ramp bill pay) or entry is fully manual. Tools write company_systems.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text/boolean + tool name. 'None, fully manual' is a valid recorded answer and a pain marker at volume.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: Bill.com reads them; Dext; we scan into; no, all manual; AI capture
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: A scanner that produces PDFs is not capture tech (no data extraction); record as manual with scanning.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Bill.com grabs maybe 80% of the fields, we fix the rest' -> Bill.com capture (~80% accuracy stated).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We scan everything to a shared drive' -> document storage, entry still manual.

Field Definitions.Question: How does your purchasing process work today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Pre-spend process: who can buy, how purchases are initiated and approved before the bill arrives.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: initiation -> approval -> ordering, as stated.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: to buy something you; purchase approval; we just buy and expense; managers can spend up to
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: 'No process, people just buy' is a finding, record it. Bill approval is ap_approval_process.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Managers buy what they need under $1k, above that they text me' -> informal; $1k threshold; text-based approval (control gap marker).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'I approve the bills before they're paid' -> AP approval, not purchasing.

Field Definitions.Question: Do you use purchase requisitions?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether a formal requisition step (request-before-order) exists.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Boolean + tooling in notes.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: requisitions; purchase requests; reqs go through; nobody submits a req
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: A verbal ask is not a requisition system; record false with the informal-process note. Don't infer from PO usage; reqs and POs are distinct steps.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Reqs in a Google Form, then ops approves' -> true; Google Form based.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'They just ask me' -> false; informal.

Field Definitions.Question: Do you use purchase orders?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether POs are issued to vendors, and coverage (all spend, inventory only, rarely).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Boolean + coverage in notes.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we cut POs; PO number; only for inventory buys; we never PO
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Receiving against POs (3-way match) is a bonus detail worth capturing in notes when stated. Customer POs received (sales side) are not this.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'POs for inventory purchases only, nothing else' -> true; coverage: inventory only.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Customers send us POs' -> sales-side, skip.

Field Definitions.Question: How are expense reports handled?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Employee expense flow: submission method, approval, reimbursement, card-vs-out-of-pocket split.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: tool + flow. Tools (Expensify, Concur, Ramp) write company_systems.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: expense reports in; Expensify; they email receipts; reimburse through payroll; nobody submits on time
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Corporate card reconciliation overlaps cc_rec_sentiment; link shared quotes. Mileage/per-diem specifics are notes, not separate fields.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Receipts get stapled to a printed form, approved by the manager, reimbursed in payroll two weeks later' -> paper-based; manager approval; payroll reimbursement (pain candidate).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'The Amex rec is painful' -> cc_rec_sentiment.

Field Definitions.Question: Do you carry inventory, and if so, what type (buy-to-sell, manufacturing, or supplies)?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: GATE for the section. Whether inventory exists on the balance sheet and its nature: buy-to-sell (distribution), manufactured goods, or internal supplies only.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Enum: none | buy_to_sell | manufacturing | supplies_only | mixed, + description. 'Supplies only' typically gates the rest of the section OFF.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we stock; we carry inventory; buy and resell; we make; just shop supplies; no inventory
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Consigned or customer-owned stock is not their inventory; capture the nuance verbatim. Service companies saying 'truck stock' may be supplies_only; clarify via follow-up rather than assuming.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'We buy parts and resell them, about $2M on the shelf' -> buy_to_sell; ~$2M carrying value noted.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We keep office supplies in a closet' -> supplies_only; section gates off.

Field Definitions.Question: Can you walk me through the full process from purchasing raw materials to selling a finished product?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The procure-to-sell narrative: buying, receiving, storage, transformation (if any), fulfillment. Accumulates across quotes like invoicing_process_end_to_end.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text narrative, every step quote-traced; gaps stay gaps.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we buy from; receive into; it sits in; then we build; ships from
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Never bridge unstated steps. Drop-ship arrangements (never touching stock) are a distinct flow worth capturing verbatim.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quotes -> 'PO to supplier -> receive at main warehouse -> picked per job -> tech installs' (each step traced).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Inserting 'then presumably QC checks it' -> fabricated; never write.

Field Definitions.Question: How are you tracking and costing inventory today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Current tracking mechanism (system, spreadsheet, physical-only) and how cost is assigned today (the method itself goes to inventory_costing_method).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: tracking tool + process. Tool names write company_systems.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: tracked in; a spreadsheet of stock; Fishbowl; we count and adjust; honestly we don't really track
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: 'We don't track it' is a finding, record it. Costing METHOD (FIFO etc.) routes to inventory_costing_method when stated.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Quantities live in Fishbowl, value is a quarterly true-up JE' -> Fishbowl (quantities); quarterly valuation true-up (control gap marker).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We're FIFO' -> costing method field.

Field Definitions.Question: How many warehouses do you have?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Count of physical stocking locations (warehouses, stocking branches; trucks if they track truck stock as locations). Canonical home: deal_sizing.warehouse_count (new column).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Number. Truck-stock counted only if the prospect frames trucks as stock locations; note the framing.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: N warehouses; N stocking locations; main DC plus N branches; every truck carries stock
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Offices and storefronts without stock are not warehouses. Entity count is unrelated; never cross-infer.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Main warehouse in Atlanta plus three branch stockrooms' -> 4.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Twelve offices' -> locations, not warehouses.

Field Definitions.Question: How often are inventory counts performed?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Physical count cadence: annual full count, cycle counts, never.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text normalized: annual | quarterly | monthly | cycle_counting | never, + detail.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we count once a year; cycle counts; full physical at year-end; haven't counted since
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: 'Should count more' is aspiration. Shrinkage complaints are pain candidates linked here.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Full count every December, that's it' -> annual.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We really need cycle counting' -> desired, note as gap.

Field Definitions.Question: Are inventory counts manual or technology-driven?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: How counts are executed: paper sheets, barcode scanners, RF guns, app-based.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Enum: manual | barcode | rf_scanners | app, + detail.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: clipboards; barcode scanners; we scan; paper count sheets; count in the app
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Owning scanners unused for counts doesn't make counts technology-driven; the stated process governs.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Two days of clipboards and rekeying the sheets' -> manual; rekey step noted (pain candidate).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We have scanners somewhere' -> ambiguous; partial.

Field Definitions.Question: How does replenishment work today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: How restock decisions happen: gut feel, min/max, system-suggested, vendor-managed.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: trigger + decider + mechanism.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we reorder when; min max; the system tells us; Joe eyeballs the shelf; vendor manages
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Reorder POINTS specifically route to uses_reorder_points (boolean); this is the broader process. One quote often fills both; link it.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'The warehouse manager eyeballs it and texts the buyer' -> informal/visual; person-dependent (risk marker).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Min/max in Fishbowl' -> also sets uses_reorder_points=true; link quote to both.

Field Definitions.Question: Do you use reorder points?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether quantitative reorder triggers (min/max, ROP) are configured and used.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Boolean + where configured.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: reorder points; min max levels; when it hits N we buy
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Intending to set them up is false-with-note. Manager intuition is not a reorder point.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Min/max on the A items only' -> true; partial coverage noted.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We know roughly when to reorder' -> false; intuition-based.

Field Definitions.Question: Do you use serialization?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether individual units are tracked by serial number (distinct from lot tracking).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Boolean. Lot tracking, if stated, recorded in notes as lot (not serial).
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: serial numbers; serialized; we track each unit; lot numbers
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Lot/batch tracking is NOT serialization; record accurately, the distinction is product-functional. Warranty registration by serial without operational tracking: capture the nuance.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Every unit has a serial we track from receipt to install' -> true.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We track lots for recalls' -> lot tracking; serialization false unless also stated.

Field Definitions.Question: Do you use kits?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether items are sold/assembled as kits or bundles (kitted SKUs, light assembly into sellable bundles).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Boolean + kit nature in notes (sales kits vs assembled kits).
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: kits; bundles; we kit; assembled into a package
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Manufacturing BOMs are manufacturing_type territory; a kit is pick-and-bundle. If they use 'kit' to mean full assembly, capture verbatim and route per the described process.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'We sell starter kits, pick five SKUs into a box' -> true; sales kits.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We build units from 40 components' -> manufacturing/BOM, not kitting.

Field Definitions.Question: What costing method do you use?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Inventory costing method: FIFO, LIFO, weighted/moving average, standard, specific identification.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Enum normalized to method names; 'don't know' is partial with a CFO follow-up task (common answer).
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: FIFO; average cost; standard cost; whatever QuickBooks does
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: 'Whatever the system does' is partial, not average-cost: capture verbatim, task to confirm (QB default is average, but stating that for them would be inference).
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'FIFO, the auditors require it' -> FIFO.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Whatever QuickBooks defaults to' -> partial; follow-up task; do NOT write 'average'.

Field Definitions.Question: When reporting on inventory, what metrics matter most to you?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The inventory measures they manage by: turns, carrying value, fill rate, dead stock, margin by item.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List of metrics, prospect's words.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we watch turns; dead stock; fill rate; what's sitting too long; margin by SKU
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Metrics they CAN'T get today are also desired_reporting candidates; tag current vs desired per quote.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Turns by category, and I want to know what hasn't moved in 90 days' -> [turns by category (current), 90-day dead stock (desired)].
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Rep: 'Most distributors watch turns' -> nothing without prospect confirmation.

Field Definitions.Question: If you manufacture, is it assembly or true manufacturing?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: SUB-GATE. Nature of production: light assembly (kit/configure) vs true manufacturing (transformation, BOM depth, routing).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Enum: none | assembly | true_manufacturing | mixed, + description.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we assemble; light assembly; we machine; multi-level BOM; fabrication
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Outsourced manufacturing (contract manufacturers) is its own nuance: they may need PO/landed-cost handling, not production. Capture verbatim.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'We assemble units from purchased components, no fabrication' -> assembly.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Our contract manufacturer in Texas builds it' -> outsourced; not internal manufacturing; note structure.

Field Definitions.Question: Does manufacturing follow an assembly line or multi-day or multi-week processes?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Production flow shape: continuous/line, job-shop, long-cycle builds (multi-day/week WIP).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: style + cycle time as stated. Long WIP cycles are a WIP-accounting signal worth flagging.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: down the line; each build takes N days; job shop; batches
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Applies only when manufacturing_type is assembly/true; otherwise skip. Lead time from VENDORS is procurement, not production cycle.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'A unit takes about two weeks on the floor' -> long-cycle (~2 weeks WIP).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Parts take six weeks to arrive' -> vendor lead time, not production style.

Field Definitions.Question: Is serialization used in manufacturing?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether serials are assigned/tracked during production (as-built records), distinct from sales-side serialization.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Boolean + at what stage assigned.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: serialized on the line; as-built; we assign serials when
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Sales-side serialization already captured does not imply production serialization; ask-level distinction, keep separate.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Serial gets etched at final assembly and logged' -> true; assigned at final assembly.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: (uses_serialization true from sales context) -> do not auto-set this; separate fact.

Field Definitions.Question: How is labor costing handled?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether/how labor is captured into product or job cost: time tracking to jobs, standard labor rates, absorbed in overhead, not captured.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: capture method + rate basis. 'Not captured' is a finding.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: labor goes to the job; standard rate per hour; we don't cost labor; time clocks feed
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Payroll processing is not labor costing. Wanting job-level labor visibility is desired state and a pain candidate.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Techs clock to jobs in ServiceTitan but it never hits the financials' -> captured operationally, not costed financially (gap finding).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Payroll is biweekly' -> payroll process, not costing.

Field Definitions.Question: What other inventory challenges exist today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Open-capture for inventory pains not covered above (shrinkage, landed cost, returns, obsolescence). Each is a pain candidate.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List; each quantified item links a pain row.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: our biggest inventory headache; shrinkage; landed cost; returns pile up; we write off
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Already-captured bottlenecks should link, not duplicate (dedup layer applies). Rep-suggested challenges unconfirmed are nothing.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'We wrote off $80k of dead stock last year' -> obsolescence pain, quantified $80k/yr; pain row.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Rep: 'Landed cost is usually a mess' Prospect: 'maybe' -> nothing.

Field Definitions.Question: What types of projects do you run?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: GATE for the section. The kinds of projects (client engagements, construction jobs, internal capital projects, grants).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: List. Empty/none gates the section off.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: our projects are; engagements; jobs; we run grants as projects
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Using 'project' loosely for initiatives without financial tracking may not gate the section on; the test is whether money is tracked per project. Capture the quote and judge by that test.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Every client engagement is a project with its own budget' -> client engagements (financially tracked); gate ON.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We have a project to redo the website' -> internal initiative, not project accounting; does not gate on alone.

Field Definitions.Question: How is project billing handled?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: How project work converts to invoices: milestone, percent-complete, T&M, fixed-fee schedules, retainage.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text per project type if they differ. Retainage stated is a strong vertical signal; flag it.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we bill milestones; monthly T&M; fixed fee up front; retainage held
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: General invoicing process is invoicing_ar_process; this is the project-specific layer. Don't duplicate; link shared quotes.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: '30% up front, 60% at delivery, 10% retainage for 90 days' -> milestone + retainage structure.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Invoices go out of QB' -> general AR mechanics.

Field Definitions.Question: How is time entry captured?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: How project hours are recorded: tool, cadence, compliance reality ('nobody submits until month-end' is the finding).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: tool + cadence + compliance color. Tools write company_systems.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: time goes into; Harvest; timesheets weekly; nobody fills them out until
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Payroll time clocks for hourly wages are not project time entry unless they feed job costing; the destination decides.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Harvest, supposedly daily, realistically the Friday panic' -> Harvest; weekly-at-best compliance (data-quality marker).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Hourly guys punch a clock for payroll' -> payroll time, unless stated to feed jobs.

Field Definitions.Question: How is revenue recognized on projects?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Rec method for project revenue: POC (input/output method), milestone, completed contract, as-billed.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text normalized to method names. 'As-billed' stated is a 606-risk flag worth noting verbatim.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: percentage of completion; we recognize when we bill; at completion; based on cost incurred
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Same billing-vs-recognition trap as revenue_recognition_method: billing schedule answers do not establish rec method; mark partial and task it.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'POC off cost incurred, the auditors check it' -> POC (cost-input).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We bill monthly' -> billing, not rec; partial.

Field Definitions.Question: How is project costing managed?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: What costs hit projects (labor, materials, subs, overhead allocation) and where that lives.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: cost components captured + tooling.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: costs hit the job; we job-cost; subs get coded to; overhead allocated at N%
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Wanting true job cost is desired state and a pain candidate. Labor specifics overlap labor_costing for manufacturers; for project businesses this is the home.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Materials and subs get coded to jobs, labor never makes it' -> partial job costing; labor gap (finding + pain candidate).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We'd kill for real job margins' -> desired; pain candidate; not current process.

Field Definitions.Question: How much visibility do you have into current project performance?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: What they can see about in-flight projects today (real-time margin, only-at-completion, nothing until the client complains).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text; lag and blind spots verbatim.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we only know at the end; can't see margin until; real-time we have nothing; the PM keeps a spreadsheet
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Visibility into the PIPELINE of projects (sales) is not delivery performance visibility. Keep scoped to financial/delivery performance.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'We find out a job lost money when it closes, months later' -> completion-lag visibility only (pain candidate).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We can see what's in the sales pipeline' -> sales visibility, skip.

Field Definitions.Question: How does that compare to target or goal performance?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether they compare project actuals to budget/target and how (budget-vs-actual per job, margin targets).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: comparison mechanism + targets if stated.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: against budget; target margin is N%; we don't really compare; variance review
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Having targets without comparing actuals is the finding; capture both halves as stated.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Target is 35% margin but we only check it at year-end across everything' -> 35% target; no per-job comparison (gap).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We want to start budgeting jobs' -> desired; not current.

Field Definitions.Question: Approximately how many fixed assets do you have?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Approximate count of tracked fixed assets. Canonical home: deal_sizing.fixed_assets.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Number. Dollar value stated instead of count goes to notes (don't convert). Ranges: midpoint + range note.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: N assets; a few hundred on the schedule; the depreciation schedule has N lines
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Asset VALUE is not asset count. Leased equipment under ASC 842 may or may not be on their schedule; capture as stated, don't reclassify.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Schedule's got about 400 lines' -> 400.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: '$3M of equipment' -> value, notes only; count remains unknown.

Field Definitions.Question: Are fixed assets managed in-house or by a CPA?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Who maintains the asset register and depreciation: internal team, external CPA, or split (books internal, tax CPA).
