Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Enum: in_house | cpa | split, + detail.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: our CPA keeps the schedule; we track in Excel; controller maintains; CPA does tax depreciation
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: CPA doing TAX depreciation while books are internal = split, a common and meaningful answer; don't collapse it to 'cpa'.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'We keep book depreciation, the CPA runs tax' -> split.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Our CPA does our taxes' -> ambiguous; partial.

Field Definitions.Question: What depreciation method is used?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Book depreciation method(s): straight-line, declining balance, units of production.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text normalized to method names; per-class differences noted.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: straight line; double declining; we depreciate over N years
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Tax methods (MACRS, Section 179, bonus) are tax-side; if mentioned, they belong in book_vs_tax_depreciation, not here.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Straight line, mostly five and seven year lives' -> straight-line; 5/7-yr lives.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We take bonus depreciation' -> tax method; route to book_vs_tax.

Field Definitions.Question: How do you handle book versus tax depreciation?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether separate book and tax depreciation are maintained and by whom; or single set of books.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: arrangement + who maintains tax side.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: two sets; book and tax; CPA handles tax depreciation; we only keep one
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: 'CPA does taxes' alone doesn't establish dual tracking; partial unless the depreciation split is stated.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Book is straight-line with us, CPA maintains MACRS for the return' -> dual; tax via CPA.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Taxes are outsourced' -> partial.

Field Definitions.Question: Do you maintain a fixed asset schedule?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether a maintained asset register exists, and where (Excel, system module, CPA's file).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Boolean + location. 'The CPA has one we never see' = true with an access-gap note.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: the schedule; asset register; it's an Excel file; CPA has it
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: An insurance equipment list is not an accounting asset schedule; capture as stated, mark partial if that's all that exists.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Excel schedule the controller updates quarterly' -> true; Excel, quarterly.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Insurance has our equipment list' -> partial; not an accounting register.

Field Definitions.Question: Do you make allocations across entities, departments, or other dimensions?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: GATE. Whether shared costs are allocated (overhead, corporate costs, shared services) across entities/departments/dimensions.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Boolean + what gets allocated.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: we allocate; spread across; corporate gets charged out; overhead allocation; we split rent between
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Intercompany BILLING (management fees) is intercompany_billing; allocations are accounting distributions. The prospect may describe a fee that IS their allocation mechanism; capture verbatim and link to both if genuinely both.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Corporate overhead gets spread to the nine entities by revenue' -> true; overhead by revenue basis.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'Each entity pays its own bills' -> likely false; record the statement.

Field Definitions.Question: Can you walk me through how allocations are done today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The mechanics: basis (revenue, headcount, square footage), frequency, tooling (Excel + JE is the common answer), effort.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: basis + frequency + mechanism. Effort quantified links a pain row.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: based on headcount; monthly allocation JE; the spreadsheet calculates; takes a day to book
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Only applies when uses_allocations is true. Wanting to START allocating is desired state; gate stays per current state with the desire noted.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Revenue-based, computed in Excel, booked as one monthly JE, half a day every month' -> revenue basis; Excel + manual JE; ~0.5 day/month (pain row).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We should be allocating IT costs' -> desired; not current process.

Field Definitions.Question: What does your budgeting process look like today?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: The annual/rolling budget process: who builds it, in what tool, on what cycle, with what participation.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text: owner + tool + cycle + participation.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: budget season; we build it in Excel; each manager submits; takes us N months; rolling forecast
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: FORECASTING (in-year reprojection) vs budgeting (the plan): capture both if both described, labeled. Wanting a budget process is a finding if none exists.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'CFO builds it in Excel over two months, entity managers email their numbers in' -> Excel; CFO-owned; ~2-month cycle; email-based inputs.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We reforecast quarterly' -> forecasting cadence; capture labeled, distinct from the budget build.

Field Definitions.Question: What are budget values based on?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: How budget numbers are derived: prior year +/- %, zero-based, driver-based (headcount, units), top-down targets.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text normalized: prior_year_adjusted | zero_based | driver_based | top_down | mixed, + detail.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: last year plus; zero based; driven off headcount; the board hands down a number
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: Aspirations to move driver-based are desired state. The basis may differ by line (revenue driver-based, opex prior-year): capture the split.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Honestly last year plus 5%, except payroll which we build from the roster' -> mixed: prior-year-adjusted opex, driver-based payroll.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We want to get to driver-based' -> desired.

Field Definitions.Question: How do you manage version control?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: How budget versions/iterations are managed: file naming chaos, single master, system-managed versions. 'FINAL_v7_REALLYFINAL.xlsx' stories are the classic pain quote.
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Text; chaos described verbatim is the value.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: versions; v1 v2 v3; which file is final; we lock the budget; everyone has their own copy
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: This only matters as stated; don't manufacture version pain from the mere fact they use Excel.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'There are six versions on the shared drive and we argued in the board meeting about which was final' -> version chaos (pain row candidate).
Field Definitions.Bad Example: (uses Excel, no version complaint stated) -> not_discussed; do not infer pain.

Field Definitions.Question: Do you perform scenario planning?
Field Definitions.Canonical Definition: Whether multiple scenarios/what-ifs are modeled (best/worst case, hiring scenarios, M&A cases).
Field Definitions.Type & Normalization: Boolean + scenario types in notes.
Field Definitions.Positive Signals: scenarios; best case worst case; we model what happens if; sensitivity
Field Definitions.Negative Signals / Anti-patterns: A single contingency conversation is not a scenario-planning practice; the test is a maintained practice. Desire to scenario-plan is desired state.
Field Definitions.Good Example: Quote: 'Three cases every year: base, stretch, and the bank covenant case' -> true; three maintained cases.
Field Definitions.Bad Example: Quote: 'We talked about what a recession would do' -> ad hoc discussion; false with note.

Core Entities.Canonical Definition: A problem the prospect currently EXPERIENCES, stated by a prospect-side speaker, in their business operations or finance function. Must be present-tense reality, not risk, desire, or hypothesis.
Core Entities.Row & Normalization Rules: One row per distinct underlying problem. Quantification (annual_cost / annual_hours) only from explicit prospect statements or simple arithmetic on stated numbers (2 days/week x 50 weeks), with the conversion noted. category from the controlled list; affected_team and mentioned_by captured when stated.
Core Entities.Positive Signals: what kills us; we waste; takes forever; error-prone; we can't; manual; my team spends
Core Entities.Anti-patterns: NOT pains: desires ('we want dashboards' -> ideal/desired), risks not yet experienced ('we might outgrow it'), rep assertions, research-derived industry pains never voiced by the prospect, and restatements of an existing pain (dedup: enrich the existing row).
Core Entities.Good Example: Quote: 'My controller spends two days a week keying AP' -> pain: manual AP entry; annual_hours ~800 (2d x 8h x 50wk, conversion noted); affected_team: accounting.
Core Entities.Bad Example: Quote: 'Companies like ours usually struggle with consolidation' (rep) -> nothing; rep speech.

Core Entities.Canonical Definition: A force or event actively DRIVING change: something happening (or recently happened) that creates the need to act. Acquisition, growth, new leadership, system end-of-life, funding event, regulatory change, audit finding.
Core Entities.Row & Normalization Rules: One row per distinct force. category + urgency from stated timeline pressure; impact from stated consequences. Research-sourced catalysts allowed ONLY with citation (e.g., press release of an acquisition) and remain unverified until voiced on a call.
Core Entities.Positive Signals: we just acquired; growing fast; new CFO; our PE firm wants; the system sunsets; we raised
Core Entities.Anti-patterns: NOT catalysts: pains (current suffering without a driving force), compelling events (consequences of inaction), generic ambitions ('we want to grow'), or the rep's narrative of why they should buy.
Core Entities.Good Example: Quote: 'We closed two acquisitions this year and the board wants consolidated numbers by Q3' -> catalysts: acquisition activity; board reporting mandate (urgency: Q3).
Core Entities.Bad Example: Quote: 'Close is painful' -> pain, not catalyst.

Core Entities.Canonical Definition: The bad thing that happens if the prospect does NOT change: the consequence of inaction, with a date or trigger where stated. The Sage canon definition; the inverse of a catalyst.
Core Entities.Row & Normalization Rules: One row per consequence. event_date when a date/trigger is stated; strength from the stated severity and specificity; verified=true only when prospect-voiced (research can propose CE candidates only as hypotheses, never as CE rows).
Core Entities.Positive Signals: if we don't; by [date] we have to; the bank requires; we lose the contract unless; can't survive another year-end like
Core Entities.Anti-patterns: NOT CEs: catalysts (drivers), soft preferences ('we'd like it before busy season' is timing color unless a consequence is attached), vendor-created urgency (rep's discount deadline is not the prospect's CE).
Core Entities.Good Example: Quote: 'If we can't produce audited consolidations by June the credit line doesn't renew' -> CE: credit-line non-renewal; date: June; strength: high.
Core Entities.Bad Example: Quote: 'Pricing goes up next quarter' (rep) -> vendor urgency; never a CE.

Core Entities.Canonical Definition: A standard the prospect states they will judge vendors against: must-haves, evaluation factors, comparison dimensions.
Core Entities.Row & Normalization Rules: One row per criterion; importance from stated weight ('non-negotiable' vs 'nice to have'); our_position filled only from evidence, else Unknown.
Core Entities.Positive Signals: has to have; must; we're comparing on; what matters to us is; deal-breaker
Core Entities.Anti-patterns: NOT criteria: ideal-solution color without pass/fail weight, the rep's differentiators recited back, process steps ('we'll do demos' is decision_process).
Core Entities.Good Example: Quote: 'Multi-entity consolidation is non-negotiable, and it has to talk to ServiceTitan' -> two criteria, both must-have.
Core Entities.Bad Example: Quote: 'Your dimensions thing seems cool' -> reaction, not a stated criterion; partial at most.

Core Entities.Canonical Definition: A software system the company currently uses (is_current) or states it needs (is_needed), with category, and integration purpose when stated.
Core Entities.Row & Normalization Rules: Natural key: system_name + category per deal; match-before-insert (NetSuite vs 'NetSuite ERP' = same row). confirmed=true only when prospect-voiced; research rows stay confidence-tagged until confirmed.
Core Entities.Positive Signals: we use; we're on; runs on; we need it to talk to
Core Entities.Anti-patterns: NOT systems: competitors under evaluation (deal_competitors), clients' systems, generic tool mentions with no business role (Slack small talk).
Core Entities.Good Example: Quote: 'Field ops runs on ServiceTitan' -> ServiceTitan, category operational, is_current, confirmed.
Core Entities.Bad Example: Quote: 'NetSuite quoted us last month' -> competitor.

Core Entities.Canonical Definition: A threat to THE DEAL (not to the prospect's business): competitive bias, no access to power, timeline slippage, budget uncertainty, champion weakness.
Core Entities.Row & Normalization Rules: One row per risk; category + severity from evidence; status open by default. AI may write quote-backed risks (e.g., prospect states the CFO is NetSuite-biased); pattern-inferred risks without quotes belong in deal_hypotheses, not here.
Core Entities.Positive Signals: the CFO prefers; we've been burned by; no budget approved yet; timeline depends on
Core Entities.Anti-patterns: NOT risks: the prospect's business problems (pains), generic deal-stage facts, hypotheses without quote backing (those go to deal_hypotheses).
Core Entities.Good Example: Quote: 'Our CFO came from a NetSuite shop and loves it' -> risk: competitive bias at economic buyer; severity high; quote-backed.
Core Entities.Bad Example: AI pattern: 'no exec sponsor identified yet' with no quote -> deal_hypotheses, not deal_risks.

Core Entities.Canonical Definition: Role-in-deal facts about a person: champion/EB/signer status, influence, alignment, sentiment, reporting line. Identity facts (name, title) may come from research with citation; ROLE facts require call evidence.
Core Entities.Row & Normalization Rules: Match-before-insert on name/email (Apollo rows enrich, never duplicate). is_champion/is_economic_buyer/is_signer set only on quote-backed evidence; otherwise hypothesis territory.
Core Entities.Positive Signals: I report to; the decision is mine; I'll champion this internally; final sign-off is
Core Entities.Anti-patterns: NOT role facts: title-based inference (CFO does not equal economic buyer without evidence: that inference is a deal_hypotheses row), Apollo seniority labels as influence claims.
Core Entities.Good Example: Quote: 'Whatever we pick, Senake signs it' -> Senake: is_signer=true, quote-backed.
Core Entities.Bad Example: Apollo: 'Senake Gajamera, CFO' -> identity fact (cited); does NOT set is_economic_buyer.

Core Entities.Canonical Definition: An SC-managed record that a Sage Intacct module is recommended for this deal and/or was demonstrated. Recommendations may be AI-SUGGESTED from verified discovery facts but only become recommended on SC/AE confirmation.
Core Entities.Row & Normalization Rules: One row per module per deal; is_recommended / is_demoed independently togglable; demoed links the demo conversation; recommended_reason references the driving discovery facts; maps to pricebook SKUs via the module reference list.
Core Entities.Positive Signals: n/a (human/AI-suggest surface, not transcript-extracted; demo detection may set is_demoed candidates from demo-call transcripts for confirmation)
Core Entities.Anti-patterns: AI never sets is_recommended directly; suggestions only. Demo detection proposes, SC confirms.
Core Entities.Good Example: inventory_type=buy_to_sell + warehouse_count=4 -> AI suggests Inventory + Order Entry modules; SC confirms -> is_recommended.
Core Entities.Bad Example: AI auto-marking modules recommended without confirmation -> forbidden.

Universal Rules.Statement: No value is written without a verbatim quote and speaker (transcript) or URL citation (research). No quote = field stays Unknown / not_discussed.
Facts about the prospect's business require a prospect-side speaker stating or explicitly confirming. Rep-stated facts with silence or weak acknowledgment are partial at most.
Anything reasoned rather than stated goes to deal_hypotheses, never to fact fields. This includes title-based role inference and industry-pattern pains.

Every field is CURRENT STATE unless the definition says otherwise. Desires route to ideal_solution / desired_reporting / success_definition. Aspirational phrasing ('we want', 'we should', 'ideally') is the routing signal.
Manually entered values are never overwritten by extraction. Contradicting evidence files a field_suggestions row with full provenance.

Every write classifies as new_fact / confirmation / changed_fact against the prior value provided in context. changed_fact records both values and surfaces qualifying-spine changes on the deal timeline.
Each fact has one canonical storage home (see architecture doc field map). Quotes may link to multiple fields when one statement genuinely answers several, but the same fact never writes two homes.
Ambiguous or incomplete answers write status=partial with the quote and generate a follow-up task. Partial never guesses the value.
A numeric value must appear in its quote or be a flagged unit conversion (weeks to business days, weekly to monthly). The edge function rejects numeric writes failing this containment check.
Quantified functional answers that evidence a problem link to a deal_pain_points row (existing or proposed) via pain_point_id, subject to match-before-insert dedup.
Section gate fields (inventory_type, project_types, uses_allocations) control whether the gated fields run. Gated-off fields are not_applicable, not not_discussed.
Granola AI summaries and notes are auxiliary context only. They can never serve as provenance; only the verbatim transcript produces quotes.

The question text in this catalog documents INTENT; it is not a script. Reps ask similar-but-different questions and prospects volunteer facts unprompted. Extraction matches the canonical definition and signals against ANY phrasing, anywhere in the call: a fact buried in a story, an answer to a differently-worded question, or an aside all count equally. Never require that the catalog question (or any question) was asked.

Independently of the field catalog, every quantified business statement by a prospect-side speaker is captured as a metric observation (value, unit, period, quote, speaker): stated metrics must never be lost because no field matched. Observations map to the metric taxonomy when unambiguous, otherwise store under the prospect's own label for review. Field values and pain quantifications link to their metric observations rather than duplicating them.
